feedback.product: 2025 KX250 mods that work (exhaust, PC piston, Twin Air PowerFlow, Twisted Development ECU, gearing, FCP Race Cups and engine mounts)
feedback.author: Steve (PulpMX)
feedback.conditions: Article says the list also applies to 2026; no track or conditions detail given.
feedback.observed: FMF Factory 4.1 and Pro Circuit Ti-6 both improve mid and top and throttle response; Pro Circuit slightly more low end, FMF slightly more mid. PC high-compression piston (needs VP T4 or equivalent) with Ti-6: more bottom torque, quicker low-rpm response, stronger mid hit, better starts (not separated from the muffler). Twin Air PowerFlow or airbox cutting: quicker response, better high-rpm breathing. Twisted Development reflash or Vortex X10: more mid pull in 2nd/3rd and more over-rev, called drastic with a muffler. One tooth larger rear (51T) for tight tracks. FCP Race Cups: on-throttle stability, more planted off-throttle; FCP engine mounts: better front-edge contact on throttle.
feedback.measured: Claims exhaust saves up to 2-3 lb; says 2025 dyno numbers favour the 2025 over the 2024 but gives no figures. No suspension settings, maps or part numbers given.

feedback.product: Rideology the App (KX) map adjustment on stock 2026 KX250
feedback.author: Ron Lawson
feedback.conditions: Testers Sean Lipanovich (about 150 lb, fast) and Mark Tilley (about 180 lb); track and weather not stated; stock bike.
feedback.observed: Fuel leaned (-3) at all throttle openings above 40 percent and spark advanced (+3) below 30 percent gave a somewhat sharper response; author says the stock map is hard to improve without other parts and that a pipe plus airbox work would allow bigger mapping gains. Showa suspension more balanced than the old KYB; both testers liked stock clickers. Very light clutch; small air filter needs frequent service.
feedback.measured: Rear sag preferred around 104 mm by both testers. 232 lb without fuel on the magazine's scale. MSRP $9,099. No clicker numbers or dyno figures.

feedback.product: 2025 KX250 race test: stock dyno vs 2024, recommended Twin Air Powerflow, Luxon bar mounts, Bolt T-plate, radiator cap
feedback.author: MXA Staff
feedback.conditions: Stock 2025 KX250; MXA test riders; settings not published.
feedback.observed: Engine weaker than 2024, especially up top, heavy off the bottom; harder shifting under load; cramped airbox; easier turning but slightly less stable at speed; soft Showa fork rides low and can feel harsh for heavier/faster riders; rear brake hard to modulate; stock bar mounts twist. Recommended: Twin Air Powerflow kit (needs its own baseplate), Luxon MX bar mounts, Bolt Hardware T-plate for seat retention, replacing the stock 1.8 kg/cm2-rated radiator cap (no brand named), and trimming plastic around the air filter.
feedback.measured: 2025 KX250: 43.7 hp at 12,500 rpm, 20.48 lb-ft at 9,200 rpm. 2024 KX250: 45.11 hp at 13,300 rpm, 21.0 lb-ft at 9,000 rpm. 2025 made less power than 2024 at every point from 6,500 rpm up. Weight 232 lb. MSRP $8,999. No clicker settings given.

feedback.product: Rideology KX app map (Broc Tickle tuned map) and fork clicker change on stock 2026 KX450
feedback.author: Ryan Nitzen
feedback.conditions: Review ride, track and weather not stated.
feedback.observed: Stock power less exciting than before; a Broc Tickle map with more fuel and ignition added bottom and mid pull and felt snappier. Fork dove deep on jump faces with that map; reviewer stiffened the fork a few clicks. Planted, stable, good in ruts, top-heavy in flat turns. Mismatched Brembo brake and Nissin clutch levers criticised. Notes a recall for crankshaft coating; 2026 models reportedly have the updated coating.
feedback.measured: Rear sag 105 mm (recommended setting, found comfortable). Claimed wet weight 248.2 lb. MSRP $10,499. Exact clicker count and map values not given.

feedback.product: 2027 KX450F / KX450FX platform changes affecting parts compatibility
feedback.author: Scott Hoffman
feedback.conditions: First look from press material and photos; no riding.
feedback.observed: Redesigned frame with longer wheelbase (pickup points appear unchanged, cast spars and engine hanger brackets differ; hangers have a single set of mounting spots unlike 2024-2026); revised swingarm; all-new longer header and muffler; Brembo front caliper and master cylinder with braided line routed behind the number plate, new Brembo rear components; revised Uni-Trak; slimmer bodywork, fender, number plate and seat, with revised shroud-to-tank mounts, so 2024-2026 bodywork is not expected to fit. Power mode button with two maps editable in RIDEOLOGY THE APP KX2; two-mode KTRC; launch control with three levels. KX450FX: 1.98 gal translucent tank, skid plate, handguards, aluminium side stand. KX250F(X) described only as new but carrying over a lot.

feedback.author: Kris Keefer
feedback.conditions: Baseline for 140-180 lb riders; part of a 2026 250 MX baseline settings roundup.
feedback.observed: Settings published as a baseline; same numbers as Keefer's 2025 KX250 baseline.
feedback.measured: Fork: spring 5.0 (printed 'N/m'), height 3 mm, compression 7 clicks out, rebound 8 clicks out. Shock: spring 54 (printed 'N/m'), sag 105 mm, high-speed compression 2.5 turns out, low-speed compression 10 clicks out, rebound 9 clicks out (page metadata omits shock rebound; body gives 9).

feedback.author: Kris Keefer
feedback.conditions: Baseline for 140-180 lb riders; 2025 250 MX baseline settings roundup.
feedback.observed: Bike stiffer than the previous frame but less harsh overall; fork can feel soft after break-in, so a slightly stiffer spring helps comfort.
feedback.measured: Fork: spring 5.0 (printed 'N/m'), height 3 mm, compression 7 out, rebound 8 out. Shock: spring 54 (printed 'N/m'), sag 105 mm, HSC 2.5 turns out, LSC 10 out, rebound 9 out.

feedback.product: 2026 KX450X long-term off-road test: maps, gearing, Precision Concepts ECU remap, DT-1 Air Flow Kit, Ride Engineering lowering link
feedback.author: Trevor Hunter
feedback.conditions: About 35 hours: West Coast rocks, roots, singletrack, desert, trees, GP and MX tracks, 2-hour sand races. Date inferred from March 2026 image uploads; no publication date in text.
feedback.observed: Smooth, torquey power; first gear tall for tight terrain and fifth short for desert. Some head shake at speed, fixed by flushing the fork in the clamps. Showa fork rides low and pitches on decel for faster/heavier riders; shock can bottom and wallow in big braking bumps and whoops. Brembo front can feel spongy. Brittle plastics, weak chain guide/slider, lower chain pad can loosen (use threadlock). Map 2 about 10-15% tamer than Map 1; traction control level 1 light, level 2 more noticeable; map change needs idling and holding the button about 3 s. Mods that helped: Precision Concepts Racing stock-ECU remap ('significant power gains'), slip-on or de-baffled stock muffler, removing the airbox top grommet and drilling the airbox cover, DT-1 Air Flow Kit, Hinson or Rekluse clutch plates, Ride Engineering lowering link or shorter shock shaft, extra chain link to move the wheel back.
feedback.measured: Sag 105-108 mm both stock and revalved. Gearing: 13/47-48 desert, 13/51-52 mountains/trees, 13/50 GP/MX. One clutch plate failure at 27 h; suggests clutch plates every 10-20 h, oil every 5-6 h. Tank 1.6 gal gives 45-60 min. MSRP $10,799. No clicker numbers, spring rates or dyno.

gaps: Kawasaki US accessory pages (kawasaki.com/en-us/shop/vehicle-accessories/...) returned server errors again; Kawasaki UK pages were readable but most product pages give no model years.

Kawasaki UK RIDEOLOGY THE APP KX: page says the app adjusts fuel and ignition maps like the earlier FI Calibration Kit and keeps maintenance logs; no app version-by-model table found. 2027 KX450 uses 'RIDEOLOGY THE APP KX2' (per Dirt Bike Test).
